title: Plausible vs Matomo
description: Plausible vs Matomo — hosted, cookieless simplicity versus self-hosted depth and data ownership for privacy-first web analytics.
verdict: Choose Plausible when you want hosted, cookieless web analytics with a short setup and predictable pageview pricing. Choose Matomo when you need GA-like reporting depth, data residency, or a self-hosted install you control.
quickAnswer: This page answers both **Plausible vs Matomo** and **Matomo vs Plausible** — same decision, either search phrasing. **Plausible** is the better fit for a marketing site that needs simple traffic reports without running servers. **Matomo** is the better fit when you need deeper web analytics, many sites, or the data on infrastructure you own.
bottomLine: Most small sites should start with **Plausible**. Move to **Matomo** when ownership, ecommerce depth, or a self-hosted requirement outweighs the extra setup. Matomo Cloud starts at $26/month for 50K hits; Plausible starts at $9/month for 10K pageviews. Self-hosted Matomo software is free, plus hosting and maintenance.

faq.question: Plausible vs Matomo: which should I pick?
faq.answer: Pick Plausible if you want a hosted, cookieless dashboard with short setup and pageview pricing. Pick Matomo if you need deeper reporting, ecommerce, many sites on one plan, or a self-hosted install you control. For a polished hosted alternative to Plausible, also look at Fathom; for Stripe revenue attribution, look at DataFast.

faq.question: Is Matomo more private than Plausible?
faq.answer: Both can be configured as privacy-friendly alternatives to GA4. Plausible is cookieless by default. Matomo supports cookieless and anonymization options, and self-hosting keeps the database on your servers. Privacy depends on the settings you turn on, not the brand name alone.

faq.question: Which is cheaper?
faq.answer: Plausible is usually cheaper for a single small site: $9/month for 10K pageviews and $19/month for 100K. Matomo Cloud starts at $26/month for 50K hits and includes up to 30 websites. Self-hosted Matomo has no license fee; you pay for the server and the time to keep it updated.

faq.question: Can I self-host both?
faq.answer: Yes. Plausible has an open-source self-hosted edition. Matomo On-Premise is the product most teams mean by self-hosted analytics. Matomo Cloud is the managed alternative if you want ownership without operating PHP and a database.

faq.question: Which replaces Google Analytics more completely?
faq.answer: Matomo. It covers ecommerce, goals, funnels, custom dimensions, and a tag manager. Plausible covers pageviews, referrers, campaigns, and a short list of goals. Use Plausible when that shorter list is the job.

editorialNotes.title: What you are actually choosing
editorialNotes.content: This is not two versions of the same dashboard. Plausible is a lightweight hosted analytics product. Matomo is a full web analytics suite you can run yourself or buy as cloud. If the weekly question is "which pages and channels brought traffic," Plausible is enough. If the weekly question is "ecommerce, custom dimensions, and data that never leaves our servers," look at Matomo.

alsoConsider.note: A polished hosted privacy analytics alternative if you like Plausible’s simplicity but want to compare vendors — referred customers get $10 off their first invoice.
Best when the question is which marketing channel drove paid customers (Stripe and similar), not only which pages got traffic.
